name: Hiram (Hiram, the craftsman from Tyre, the bronze caster who worked for Solomon)
title: The Bronze Caster from Tyre
summary: Hiram was a highly skilled craftsman and bronze caster from Tyre who was brought by King Solomon to carry out the bronze work for the temple in Jerusalem. He was the son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali and a Tyrian father, and his masterful work included the two large bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, the bronze sea, and a number of other cult objects. His craftsmanship was crucial to the decoration of Solomon's temple.

keyEvents.title: Hiram is Brought from Tyre
keyEvents.description: King Solomon sent for Hiram from Tyre, a skilled bronze caster and son of a widow from the tribe of Naphtali, to carry out all the bronze work for the temple.

keyEvents.title: Casting of the Two Bronze Pillars
keyEvents.description: Hiram cast the two large bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, which were placed in front of the temple hall. Each pillar was eighteen cubits high and had decorated capitals.

keyEvents.title: The Bronze Sea
keyEvents.description: Hiram made the great bronze sea, an enormous round basin that stood on twelve bronze oxen, used for the priests' ritual washings.

keyEvents.title: The Ten Bronze Carts and Basins
keyEvents.description: Hiram made ten bronze carts with decorated side panels and ten bronze basins that were placed on the carts, used in the service of the temple.

keyEvents.title: Other bronze articles for the temple
keyEvents.description: Hiram finished all the work he did for King Solomon: the basins, shovels and sprinkling bowls. He made all these things of burnished bronze for the Lord's house.

keyEvents.title: Parallel account in 2 Chronicles
keyEvents.description: 2 Chronicles gives a parallel account of Hiram's work and describes him as a man full of wisdom, understanding and skill in working with bronze.
